title: Finite partial sum representatives for cohomology of a coproduct on a qcqs scheme
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], I an arbitrary index type, F_i sheaves of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and S a coproduct of the F_i with inclusions iota_i [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every nonnegative p and x in H^p(X,S) [pqf-def-cohomology], there exist a finite subset J of I and y in H^p(X,B_J), where B_J is the finite biproduct of the F_j in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian], such that H^p(X,kappa_J)(y)=x. Here kappa_J is the unique map whose composite with each biproduct inclusion is iota_j. The empty finite subset is permitted.

source.place: Cohomology, Tag 01FF, label lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit, lines 3194-3211; direct-sum application in Tag 09J7, label lemma-perfect-is-compact, lines 13762-13768. Only the finite-stage existence assertion is used.

proof.text: The compact opens form a basis stable under intersections on a qcqs scheme, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] and [def-weil-spectral-space]. The whole space is compact by hypothesis.

For finite J choose the finite biproduct B_J of the F_j; these exist in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-sp-abelian]. Its underlying cofan is a coproduct. Inclusion of finite subsets gives transition maps characterized on the summands. The finite subsets are directed under union, with the empty set as an initial object. The finite-subsum colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-coproduct-finite-subsums] identifies the resulting colimit with S via its given coproduct cofan.

Apply the existence-of-stage clause of [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] at the whole space to this diagram. Cohomology is that of [pqf-def-cohomology]. Forgetting the global scalar action compares module-valued global-sections cohomology with the abelian-group-valued open cohomology at the top open: both apply sections to the same injective module resolution and take homology, and forgetting scalars preserves kernels and cokernels. Thus a class x has a representative y in H^p(X,B_J) for some finite J. For larger index universes, discard zero summands and shrink the remaining index set: choose a nonzero section of each nonzero F_i and send it by iota_i into the disjoint union of section sets of S over opens. Coproduct projections show these pairs are distinct for distinct indices, so the nonzero indices form a u-small set. Reindex by a small equivalent type, apply the recorded directed-colimit lemma there, and transport the finite subset back to I. Zero summands do not affect the coproduct or any finite biproduct.

The structural map B_J to S restricts to iota_j on every summand, hence is biproduct.desc by the coproduct universal property. This gives the stated equality. Empty J is allowed, and degree zero requires no alteration.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCohomology_finiteSubsum_representative (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (I : Type v)
    (F : I → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    (S : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) (ι : ∀ i : I, F i ⟶ S)
    (_hS : IsColimit (Cofan.mk S ι)) (p : ℕ)
    (x : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj S) :
    ∃ (J : Finset I)
      (y : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj (⨁ (fun j : J ↦ F j))),
      ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).map
        (biproduct.desc (fun j : J ↦ ι j))).hom y = x
